PullRequest.Title: check for valid account and provide option to sign in

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path is explicit: this added await reaches DefaultAccountService.getDefaultAccount(), which waits only on initBarrier, while the new contribution returns without setDefaultAccount() when product configuration or the declared provider is absent and also fails to set it when the entitlement request rejects. The manifest promise is cached, so no later caller can recover. The prevalence of custom Marketplace policy is deployment-specific, but the indefinite wait once triggered is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Pending manifest promises and downstream Marketplace IPC/network operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: A single account-initialization exit or entitlement failure leaves the one cached manifest promise pending for the entire window lifetime; every Marketplace query, install, update, and shared/remote-process consumer coalesces behind that same unresolved promise.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded Marketplace latency and permanently blocked extension operations for the affected window
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the change, a configured service URL was fetched directly and the default manifest was otherwise built immediately; manifest resolution had no dependency on account initialization completing.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: When a configured gallery URL is present, manifest resolution now awaits the default-account barrier before it can select either the configured or fallback gallery.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 89 adds `await this.defaultAccountService.getDefaultAccount()` to the configured-gallery manifest path; no account barrier existed on this path before the PR.
Findings.Title: Release the account barrier on every initialization exit
Findings.Impact: With a configured Marketplace URL, an offline/failing entitlement endpoint, missing defaultAccount product entry, or unavailable declared authentication provider prevents the barrier from opening. Opening Extensions or any install/update/query then waits forever instead of falling back to the default gallery.
Findings.Evidence: The added condition at line 89 awaits defaultAccountService.getDefaultAccount(). That method waits on initBarrier, and only setDefaultAccount() opens it. DefaultAccountManagementContribution has early returns for missing product configuration and an undeclared provider, and its awaited entitlement request can reject before setDefaultAccount() executes. ExtensionGalleryService.query() awaits this manifest before issuing its Marketplace request, while the shared/remote IPC manifest service also waits on a barrier populated only after this promise resolves.
Findings.Recommendation: Make account initialization settle the service on every terminal path: set the unavailable/null state before each early return and in a narrowly handled entitlement failure path (while logging or surfacing the error), or otherwise expose an initialization promise that always resolves. Then let manifest selection fall back to the default gallery instead of retaining a permanently pending promise.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new excluded setting has a policy definition, so this added call is non-empty on a cold first window. PolicyChannelClient turns each new-definition batch into an awaited IPC call; NativePolicyService serializes it through a throttler and creates/replaces a native watcher, while FilePolicyService performs another file read. Workspace initialization explicitly awaits policy initialization before returning. Only the exact duration is platform-dependent.
Findings.PerformanceResource: An extra IPC request plus native policy-watcher initialization or policy-file read
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is one additional serialized boundary operation per cold desktop window when this newly registered excluded policy is not already present in policiesData; warm windows with the definition already cached can skip it.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased cold-window startup latency on the configuration initialization critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: PolicyConfiguration.initialize() made one awaited updatePolicyDefinitions call for all initial configuration keys before workspace startup could continue.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Initialization now awaits the included-policy batch and then separately awaits a second excluded-policy batch, despite both key sets being available before either update.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 112 adds a separate awaited `updatePolicyDefinitions` invocation for excluded properties; the PR also adds an excluded property with a policy, guaranteeing this batch contains a new definition on the cold path.
Findings.Title: Coalesce excluded policies into the initial policy update
Findings.Impact: On the first window after launch, the new hidden Marketplace policy causes configuration startup to perform a second renderer-to-main IPC round-trip and reconstruct the OS policy watcher (or reread the policy file) before the workspace service and workbench can start.
Findings.Evidence: Line 112 adds a second sequential await. PolicyChannelClient._updatePolicyDefinitions calls the policy IPC channel; NativePolicyService._updatePolicyDefinitions imports the native module and queues createWatcher(), replacing its watcher, and FilePolicyService refreshes by reading the policy file. WorkspaceService.initialize() awaits initializeConfiguration(), which awaits this policy promise, and desktop startup awaits WorkspaceService.initialize() before creating the workbench.
Findings.Recommendation: Concatenate the default-model keys and excluded-property keys and call updatePolicyDefinitions once, then update the configuration model from that single result so registration ordering and policy values are preserved without a second boundary crossing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold desktop window startup with native or file-backed enterprise policy support
Scenarios.CriticalPath: desktop.main awaits WorkspaceService.initialize(); initializeConfiguration() awaits PolicyConfiguration.initialize(), so both sequential policy-definition updates must finish before the workspace service and workbench can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send updatePolicyDefinitions from the renderer PolicyChannelClient to the main-process policy service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: one initial batch. After: two sequential batches on the cold first window because the excluded Marketplace policy is new; warm subsequent windows may skip the second batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the default configuration keys produced an updatePolicyDefinitions IPC call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both responses are awaited by configuration initialization before workspace startup proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/replace the native OS policy watcher
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional watcher creation for the excluded-policy batch on the cold path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One watcher initialization served the initial policy batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: NativePolicyService resolves only after the watcher invokes its initial callback, so recreation extends startup latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the policy file in file-policy deployments
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional file read for the second non-empty definition batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The initial policy registration caused one refresh/read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read is awaited through policy and workspace initialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The initial registered configuration-key set plus the excluded configuration-key set. This PR contributes one excluded policy key, so the second batch has effective cardinality one on a cold first window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two calls are explicitly sequential awaits. Renderer policy updates cross IPC to a NativePolicyService throttler, which serializes watcher creation; the file-backed implementation also awaits each refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AbstractPolicyService skips the native/IPC update when a definition is already known. The new workbench-only definition is absent on the first cold window, while later windows may receive it through serialized policiesData and skip the second boundary call.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line adds a second sequential await, the new excluded policy guarantees a new definition in its target deployment, and the IPC/native/file implementations and startup awaits are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact IPC and watcher/file-read duration varies by OS, policy backend, and machine, and warm windows may avoid the second call; the added serialized boundary operation on cold startup is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable missing-coalescing regression: one initial policy batch has been split into two serialized boundary operations on the cold startup critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve and propagate a policy-configured Marketplace manifest
Scenarios.CriticalPath: WorkbenchExtensionGalleryManifestService starts manifest resolution from its constructor. With a configured URL it now waits for default-account initialization, then may fetch the entitlement document, then fetches the configured manifest, and only afterward propagates the manifest to shared and remote processes. Extension queries also await the same manifest promise.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch account entitlements with the first session access token
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One uncached GET on cold initialization when a session exists; on failure it is not retried, but leaves all manifest consumers blocked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Configured manifest resolution did not contact the entitlement endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly precedes configured Marketplace manifest selection and therefore blocks every Marketplace operation that awaits the manifest.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per window after account access is approved, coalesced by extensionGalleryManifestPromise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Non-stable configured-gallery use fetched this manifest directly without an account barrier.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before Marketplace query/install/update can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the resolved manifest to shared-process and optional remote-agent channels
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared-process call and, for remote workspaces, one remote-channel call per resolved manifest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same propagation occurred as soon as the direct/default manifest promise resolved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Downstream ExtensionGalleryManifestIPCService consumers remain behind their own barrier until these calls happen.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One configured Marketplace URL and the first authenticated session. The manifest promise coalesces all callers to one attempt per window, but every caller shares its completion or permanent non-completion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Account resolution, entitlement GET, and configured-manifest GET are serialized. All manifest consumers coalesce behind one cached promise; the shared and remote IPC updates fan out to at most two channels only after it resolves.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The manifest promise and selected manifest are cached for the window. The entitlement GET explicitly disables caching. If account initialization exits or rejects before setDefaultAccount(), its barrier never opens and the cached manifest promise remains pending with no retry or fallback.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the added await, the account barrier's sole opening point, every early/failure path, the cached manifest promise, downstream query await, and IPC barrier are all visible in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Custom Marketplace policy prevalence is deployment-specific, but missing product/provider configuration and entitlement network failure are explicit reachable exits; once triggered, the blocked duration is the window lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cleanup-lifecycle regression: account initialization can fail to release a new manifest prerequisite, producing indefinite Marketplace latency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initialize and refresh the default account shown in the Accounts menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution starts after workbench restore and waits for installed extension registration. It queries provider sessions and, when present, performs an entitlement GET before setting account status. This work is normally off the startup restore critical path, but becomes critical when the configured-gallery manifest is waiting for it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once after restore and once per matching session event; zero entitlement requests when no sessions are returned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the normal restore path, but required before a configured gallery can resolve.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One uncached request after each session query that returns at least one session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No entitlement request was performed by this contribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines the Accounts menu state and gates configured-gallery selection; otherwise runs after restore.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One startup initialization plus one refresh for each matching authentication session event. Typical session-change cardinality is small; unrelated providers are filtered.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initial operations are serialized. Matching session events invoke async handlers without a limiter and can overlap, but no realistic high-frequency source was established in the reviewed paths.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session results are delegated to the authentication provider. Entitlement responses are never cached (`disableCache: true`); account state is retained in memory after completion.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added operations and scheduling; lower for any event-burst magnitude, so no separate repeated-work finding was submitted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication providers may emit multiple change events, but the inspected code does not establish a frequent enough realistic burst to justify a separate concurrency/fan-out finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the normal one-request post-restore account check is intentional feature work, and event frequency is insufficiently established; its failure-to-settle effect on Marketplace consumers is covered by the reported barrier finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh the Extensions view after a gallery-manifest change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The view container registers a manifest-change listener that calls refresh(), which updates installed-extension contexts, reruns the current search, and may check for updates. This work would be user-visible when the view exists.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One refresh per manifest-change event and the current extension/search result set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: refresh() is invoked directly per event; search has its existing scheduling, but the changed desktop manifest implementation does not fire its new emitter in any inspected path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache behavior applies because no changed path emits the event after initial manifest selection; existing extension-workbench caches remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the listener is added and high that no current emitter fire is present; therefore no runtime performance regression is established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future emitters could make refresh expensive, but the supplied diff provides no reachable emission, so there is no concrete changed event frequency or boundary cardinality to review.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: adding the listener alone does not execute refresh work on any changed reachable path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and traced startup policy initialization, account lifecycle, Marketplace manifest/query propagation, authentication refreshes, and Extensions view refresh behavior. Submitted two findings: an indefinitely unresolved account barrier blocking Marketplace operations and a second serialized policy IPC/watcher operation on cold startup.
